notes: The booklet really builds two separate models: the Light Repair Truck (with its minifig seated in the cab) and a street lamp with traffic light on a green base plate. The lamp restarts at step 1 and is shown standing on its own base beside the truck on pages 1 and 33, so it is intentionally not connected to the truck. The minifig is connected to the truck by a contact edge.

The checker reports element 4616279 as 4 on the page and 4496442 as 2. The inventory page text lists these IDs twice, probably once in the legend and once in the grid. The steps use 4616279 two times (step 7) and the windscreen 4496442 once (step 19), so the graph keeps 2 and 1.

The inventory printed 9341 (minifig legs) and 9566 (blue steering wheel on plate). The checker rejected those IDs, so the legs use design number 970c00 and the steering wheel uses catalogue lego-3829, with colour blue. Their labels record the printed numbers.
Element IDs come from a low-resolution inventory page. Some pieces were matched to steps by shape only.

Element 241226 (2x on the inventory page) is used twice, as the ridged dark piece on the dashboard (b45) and the ridged dark piece in the arm (b64). Element 4211679 is used twice: in the second arm and in the lamp.
The red hard hat (element 383321) uses catalogue type lego-minifig-hardhat. The blue long pin uses its own element ID, lego-4514553.
Cab side panels use a bar port that clips onto the orange clip plates. The wheel hub-to-tire join uses pin/pin-hole ports.
Joined edges mostly use null ports for stud connections because the exact stud positions are not legible in the pictures. Stickers are not modelled.

The four wheels are one repeat: copies 1 and 2 attach to the pins of holder b9, copies 3 and 4 to the pins of holder b10. The two white cones with orange caps are another repeat, attached to the two studs of the yellow plate b54.
